label: Etomidate PK — Kaneda (2011)

parameters.label: effect-site equilibration rate constant (BIS)
parameters.covariate_model: ke0 = ln2 / 1.550 min = 0.4472 (t1/2 ke0 for BIS)

known_failure_modes.condition: infusion longer than ~10 min (prose; not a covariate predicate)
known_failure_modes.behavior: Fitted to brief infusions (5 mg/min to loss of eyelash reflex). The authors state the results apply only to short-term infusion of less than 10 minutes; a 2-compartment fit to minutes of data cannot describe the slow redistribution that long infusions expose.

extraction.tier_rationale: Small (n=18) healthy-volunteer NONMEM study of brief infusions; 2-compartment, absolute. The envelope (18-55 y, 50-80 kg) is from the opentiva implementation, not the abstract (a human item). The BIS PD (EC50 0.526 ug/mL, gamma 2.25) is published, but E0/Emax are not in the abstract, so no PD record is curated (never-invent).

source_review.reviewed_by: automated source cross-check (Claude Opus 5.5 via Hypnos)
source_review.method: compared against the primary-paper PubMed abstract (verbatim values) and one open implementation
sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20498288/ (abstract: V1 4.45, V2 74.90 L; CL 0.63, Q 3.16 L/min; t1/2 ke0 1.550 min)
source_review.notes: All four PK values and the t1/2 ke0 are quoted verbatim in the abstract; opentiva agrees (ke0 0.447 = ln2/1.55). Etomidate's classic Arden 1986 set (STANPUMP) is not curated: its abstract prints no parameters and only one implementation carries them. HUMAN ITEMS: confirm the envelope and whether the ke0 is BIS- or OAA/S-linked.

notes: The last IV hypnotic on the v0.1 hypnotics_iv list. Arden 1986 found that etomidate's dose requirement falls with age because the initial distribution volume contracts, not because the brain becomes more sensitive.
